chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the height of the room is above seven cubits, or he said: eight cubits, then what is above the seven and eight cubits is a meeting place (for prayer), and some of them said: a dwelling.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum height of a room for valid prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the minimum structural height (seven or eight cubits) required for a space to be considered a valid dwelling (maskun) or a proper place for prayer (muhtadiran), reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on architectural standards for ritual purity. The divergence between 'muhtadiran' (a place of presence/worship) and 'maskun' (inhabited) highlights the scholarly debate on whether the validity stems from the space's function as a prayer hall or its status as a residential unit, a nuance critical in fiqh al-bayt (jurisprudence of the house).
